info.title: Bachs API
info.description:
The Bachs API lets you accept payments, manage subscriptions, and move money across African markets.

- **Authentication:** pass your secret key as `Authorization: Bearer sk_...`. See [Authentication](/authentication) for keys, scopes, and sandbox vs production.
- **Errors:** every error returns a flat `{ "detail", "error_code", "doc_url" }`. See [Errors](/errors).
- **Pagination:** list endpoints return `{ items, pagination }`. See [Pagination](/guides/pagination).
- **Idempotency:** retry `POST` safely with the `Idempotency-Key` header. See [Idempotency](/guides/idempotency).
- **Base URLs and rate limits:** see the [Introduction](/api-reference/overview).

patch.description:
Update a destination: rename it, (de)promote it as a payout schedule's default, or restate where money lands.

`name` and `is_default` alone are safe: neither touches review status, since the default can only ever be one of your own approved destinations. Sending any routing detail (currency, type, account, wallet or phone) restates the destination in full, the same shape as `POST`; omitted routing fields fall back to what is already stored. Changing an account number, bank code, wallet, network, or phone number this way sends the destination back for review, because the approval it holds was granted for the details it is being asked to leave behind.

Common errors:
- `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`: neither `name` nor `is_default` sent, or an invalid payload for the destination type. Resolution: validate request fields and retry.
- `401 UNAUTHORIZED`: API key is missing, invalid, or revoked. Resolution: use a valid API key in the `Authorization` header.
- `404 NOT_FOUND`: `destination_id` was not found. Resolution: verify destination ID and retry.

post.description:
Replay a previously generated webhook event by creating a new outbound delivery attempt. Use this when your endpoint missed or rejected an earlier delivery and you need Bachs to send that event again.

Common errors:
- `400 BAD_REQUEST`: No supported lookup field was provided. Resolution: provide at least one of `event_id`, `charge_id`, or `reference`.
- `401 UNAUTHORIZED`: Authorization is missing, invalid, or revoked. Resolution: send a valid bearer credential.
- `404 NOT_FOUND`: No matching webhook event could be resolved for your lookup values. Resolution: verify IDs/references and retry.

event_id.description: Webhook event ID to replay directly.

charge_id.description: Charge ID used to resolve the latest webhook event for that charge.

reference.description: Checkout reference used to resolve charge and replay latest webhook event.

schema.description: Provide at least one identifier. If `event_id` is provided, that exact event is replayed. Otherwise, the replay target is resolved by `charge_id` or `reference`.

200.description: Success - replay request accepted and a new delivery attempt was created.

event_id.description: The event that was replayed. It keeps its original ID, so a replay is a fresh delivery of the same event rather than a new event.

attempt_id.description: The delivery attempt this replay created. Look it up to see whether the delivery succeeded.

attempt_no.description: Which attempt this is for the event, counting every earlier automatic retry.

event_type.description: The type of the event that was replayed, the same value your endpoint receives in the payload.

get.description: Retrieve checkout configuration for your account context, including enabled payment methods, per-method currency toggles, and fee preference.

parameters.name: X-Account-Id
parameters.description: Account ID when acting on behalf of a sub-account.

organization_id.description: The account these settings apply to, which is the account your API key belongs to, or the account you named in `X-Account-Id`.

enabled_payment_methods.description: The methods a customer can pay with at checkout, keyed by exact corridor (`USD_CARD`, `NGN_CARD`, `NGN_BANK_TRANSFER`, `MOMO_GHS`..`MOMO_ZMW`, `CRYPTO`) -- see [payment method support](/guides/payments/payment-method-support). Each entry carries an `enabled` flag; `CRYPTO` alone additionally carries a `currencies` map (per-asset toggles), since every other corridor already names its one currency in the key itself.

fee_preference.description: Who pays the processing fee on a checkout, unless the individual checkout overrides it. `customer_pays`: the fee is added on top of the amount the customer pays, so you settle the full amount. `org_pays`: you absorb the fee and it is netted out of what settles into your balance.

available_currencies.description: Every currency each corridor is configured to accept on the platform, keyed by the same exact corridors as `enabled_payment_methods`, so you know which currencies you can switch on before you send an update.

put.description: Update checkout configuration for your account context, including enabled payment methods and fee preference.

parameters.name: X-Account-Id
parameters.description: Account ID when acting on behalf of a sub-account.

enabled_payment_methods.description: The corridors to offer at checkout, keyed by exact corridor (`USD_CARD`, `NGN_CARD`, `NGN_BANK_TRANSFER`, `MOMO_GHS`..`MOMO_ZMW`, `CRYPTO`) -- see [payment method support](/guides/payments/payment-method-support). Each entry you send must carry an `enabled` boolean; `CRYPTO` additionally accepts a `currencies` map of per-asset booleans. This replaces the stored configuration wholesale: a corridor you omit resets to its platform default rather than keeping its current state.

fee_preference.description: Who pays the processing fee on a checkout from now on. `customer_pays`: the fee is added on top of the amount the customer pays, so you settle the full amount. `org_pays`: you absorb the fee and it is netted out of what settles into your balance. Omit the field to leave the current preference untouched.

schema.description: Provide one or both fields: `enabled_payment_methods` and `fee_preference`.

organization_id.description: The account whose settings were updated, which is the account your API key belongs to, or the account you named in `X-Account-Id`.

enabled_payment_methods.description: The stored configuration after the update, keyed by exact corridor. The update replaces the whole map, so this returns the corridors you sent and nothing else. Read it back to confirm which corridors are now live at checkout.

fee_preference.description: Who now pays the processing fee on a checkout. `customer_pays`: the fee is added on top of the amount the customer pays, so you settle the full amount. `org_pays`: you absorb the fee and it is netted out of what settles into your balance.

message.description: A confirmation string for the update. Do not branch on it, since the returned `enabled_payment_methods` and `fee_preference` carry the state you should check.

currency.description: Base currency code (e.g., 'USD', 'NGN'). Must be a supported fiat currency.

amount.description: Base amount as decimal string. Required for a fixed price; omit for a custom (buyer-entered) or free price. Minimum 100 for `NGN`, 1 for `USD` (and per-currency minimums for other supported currencies).

price_type.description: `fixed` (default when amount is set) | `custom` (buyer enters the amount at checkout, within optional bounds, via the checkout-level set-amount) | `free` ($0).

preset_amount.description: Suggested starting amount for a custom price.

minimum_amount.description: Lower bound for a custom price.

maximum_amount.description: Upper bound for a custom price.

currency_options.description: Currency-specific pricing overrides. Keys are fiat currency codes, values are decimal amount strings.

product_id.description: Product ID to include in checkout.

quantity.description: Number of units for the product item.

amount.description: Chosen amount for a pay-what-you-want price. For a catalog CUSTOM product, or an ad-hoc CUSTOM price (pre-filling the buyer's amount).

AdhocPriceInput.description: Ad-hoc price override for this checkout only (no product is created). Priced in the product's primary currency. Supports the same price types as catalog prices: `fixed`, `custom`, `free`.

price_type.description: `fixed` sets a set amount via `amount`. `custom` is pay-what-you-want, bounded by `minimum_amount`/`maximum_amount` with an optional `preset_amount`; the buyer picks the amount at checkout. `free` is a $0 line that completes without payment; on a recurring product it creates a free subscription (no card, renews with no charge).

amount.description: The price, for a `fixed` ad-hoc price. Required for `fixed`; not valid for `custom`.

preset_amount.description: Suggested starting amount for a `custom` ad-hoc price.

minimum_amount.description: Lower bound for a `custom` ad-hoc price.

maximum_amount.description: Upper bound for a `custom` ad-hoc price.

name.description: Customer full name.

oneOf.description: Checkout with a cart of catalog products (each item may override its price via `pricing`).
Pure checkout with a raw amount and currency, no products.

billing_currency.description: Optional checkout billing currency. If omitted, defaults to product pricing currency.

payment_method_types.description: Restricts the checkout to specific payment methods. Values are exact payment-method corridors, not payment types: `USD_CARD` and `NGN_CARD` are separate corridors, as is each of the nine mobile money corridors. Valid values: `USD_CARD` (US card, USD), `NGN_CARD` (Nigerian card, NGN), `NGN_BANK_TRANSFER` (Nigerian bank transfer, NGN), `MOMO_GHS` (Ghana mobile money), `MOMO_KES` (Kenya mobile money), `MOMO_TZS` (Tanzania mobile money), `MOMO_UGX` (Uganda mobile money), `MOMO_XAF` (Central Africa CFA mobile money), `MOMO_XOF` (West Africa CFA mobile money), `MOMO_RWF` (Rwanda mobile money), `MOMO_MWK` (Malawi mobile money), `MOMO_ZMW` (Zambia mobile money), and `CRYPTO` (all supported crypto assets). A corridor you leave out is not offered. Restricting only narrows what the customer sees: it never adds a corridor your account is not already enabled for. If the restriction leaves no payable method, the request is rejected.

cancel_url.description: Where to send the customer if they cancel or abandon the checkout. Returned on the checkout so the hosted page can route back to it.

return_url.description: Deprecated alias for `success_url`, kept for backward compatibility. If both are set, `success_url` wins.

success_url.description: Where to redirect the customer after a successful payment. Bachs appends `?checkout_id=<id>`. This is the primary success-redirect field.

customer.description: Customer details for the checkout session.

product_cart.description: Catalog products to include in this checkout session. Mutually exclusive with `pricing`.

pricing.description: Raw pricing for a product-less (pure) checkout. Mutually exclusive with `product_cart`.

platform_fee.description: The platform's cut of this sale, in the base currency of the sale, taken from the merchant's proceeds rather than from Bachs's processing fee. On a destination charge, this is one of two ways to state the split: the account receives the gross minus this amount. Mutually exclusive with `transfer_data.amount`. A destination charge needs one of the two; a direct charge can set this alone to move part of its own charge up to the platform. See [Platform fees](/connect/platform-fees).

transfer_data.description: Names the account this checkout pays out to. Its presence, on its own, is what makes this a destination charge belonging to your platform rather than the account. A destination charge needs a split term: either `platform_fee` on the request root, or `transfer_data.amount` here. Omit `transfer_data` entirely, and act as the account with `X-Account-Id` instead, for a direct charge. See [Destination charges](/connect/split-payments/destination).

reference.description: Your own reference for this session, unique per account. Omit it and the session has none; use the session's `id` to track it.

expires_in_minutes.description: Minutes until the checkout session expires. Defaults to 60. After expiry the checkout URL is invalid.

destination.description: The account to transfer the sale to. Its presence, on its own, is what makes this a destination charge. It must be one of your own accounts; any other ID returns `404` so the response never confirms that an unrelated account exists.

amount.description: What the destination account receives, in the base currency of the sale. Supply this instead of `platform_fee` to fix the seller's share and let the platform absorb any variance in the total. Mutually exclusive with `platform_fee`; a request setting both is rejected with `400`.

reference.description: Your unique identifier for this refund. Must be unique per account and environment.

refund_id.description: Pass this to retrieve the refund later.

name.description: A label you choose to tell this endpoint apart from your others in the dashboard and in list responses. It is never sent to the endpoint.

name.description: Replaces the endpoint's label. Omit it to leave the current label unchanged.

It is shown in full only in this response, so store it in your secret manager now; afterwards you can only read it back from [Get Endpoint Secret](/api-reference/webhooks/get-webhook-endpoint-secret) or replace it by rotating.

WebhookEndpointSecretResponse.description: An endpoint with its current signing secret.

endpoint_id.description: Use this identifier to fetch, update, delete, or rotate the secret on this endpoint, and to scope event listings to it.

name.description: The label you gave the endpoint. It is never sent to the endpoint itself.

url.description: The HTTPS URL we POST each subscribed event to.

enabled.description: When `true`, matching events are delivered here. When `false`, events still occur on your account but nothing is sent to this URL.

event_types.description: The event types this endpoint receives, stored lowercase. Anything not listed is never delivered here.

created_at.description: When the endpoint was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC.

updated_at.description: When the endpoint was last changed, as an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC. Rotating the signing secret updates this.

secret.description: Use this to verify the `X-Bachs-Signature` header on every delivery to this endpoint and reject anything that does not match. This response and the create response are the only places it is shown in full, so treat it like a password: never log it, never put it in client-side code, and rotate it if it leaks.

event_source.description: Which account's events reach this endpoint. `account`: only your own account's events. `connect`: only the events of accounts you own. `all`: both.

date.description: The first day of the bucket, as a `YYYY-MM-DD` date in UTC. For `week` and `month` periods this is the day the bucket starts, not a range.

success.description: How many attempts in this bucket got a 2xx from your endpoint. A retry that eventually succeeds counts here as well as counting its earlier failures in `failed`.

failed.description: How many attempts in this bucket got a non-2xx response or never connected. A sustained non-zero value means your receiver is rejecting or timing out and events are being retried.

WebhookMetricsResponse.description: Delivery metrics for an endpoint over a time range.

total.description: The number of delivery attempts across the whole range, as a string. It equals the sum of `success` and `failed` over every entry in `data`, so use it to compute a success rate without re-adding the series.

period.description: How the series is bucketed. `day`: one entry per calendar day (the default, over the last 30 days when you send no dates). `week`: one entry per week. `month`: one entry per month. An unrecognised value falls back to `day`.

data.description: One entry per bucket in the range, in ascending time order. Buckets with no attempts are still returned with zero counts, so the series is safe to plot without filling gaps yourself.

WebhookEventListItem.description: A summary of a webhook event across all endpoints.

event_id.description: Pass this to [Get Event](/api-reference/webhooks/get-webhook-event) for the full payload and attempt history. It is also the `id` inside the delivered payload, so you can use it to deduplicate on your side.

event_type.description: What happened, in `resource.action` form, for example `customer.created` or `payout.paid`. Branch on this before reading the payload.

entity_type.description: The kind of resource the event is about, for example `customer`, `charge`, `payout`, `refund`, or `checkout`. It is `null` when the event carries no identifiable resource.

entity_id.description: The identifier of the resource named by `entity_type`, so you can correlate the event with your own records without opening the payload. It is `null` when the event carries no identifiable resource.

created_at.description: When the event was recorded, as an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC. Events are returned newest first by this value, not by when they were delivered.

attempts.description: How many delivery attempts your endpoints have made for this event in total. It is `0` when no endpoint was subscribed to this event type at the time.

success.description: How many of those attempts were answered with a 2xx. Anything above zero means you have received this event at least once and should have handled it idempotently.

failed.description: How many of those attempts were rejected or never connected. A non-zero value with `success` at zero means this event has not reached you yet.

last_attempt_at.description: When the most recent attempt was made, as an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC. It is `null` when the event has never been attempted.

last_attempt_status.description: How the most recent attempt ended. `pending`: queued and not yet sent. `succeeded`: your endpoint answered with a 2xx. `failed`: your endpoint answered with a non-2xx or could not be reached. It is `null` when the event has never been attempted.

last_attempt_http_status.description: The HTTP status code your endpoint returned on the most recent attempt. It is `null` when the connection never completed, for example on a DNS failure or a timeout, which is what distinguishes a transport failure from a rejection.

last_attempt_error.description: Why the most recent attempt failed, as a short diagnostic string you can act on, for example a timeout or a TLS failure. It is `null` when the attempt succeeded or none has been made.

account.description: The account the event happened on. It is your own account for your own activity, and the id of the account when the event came from one of the accounts you own, so use it to route the event to the right tenant.

WebhookEventsListResponse.description: A paginated list of webhook events.

items.description: Your account's events plus those of any accounts you own, newest first, whether or not they were ever delivered. Each entry is a summary; fetch the full payload and attempt history with [Get Event](/api-reference/webhooks/get-webhook-event).

total.description: How many events exist across your account and the accounts you own, ignoring `limit` and `offset`. Use it to decide whether another page is worth requesting.

limit.description: The page size actually applied, which is clamped to between 1 and 100 whatever you request.

offset.description: How many events were skipped before this page. Add `limit` to it to request the next page.

WebhookEndpointEventListItem.description: A summary of an event's delivery to one endpoint.

event_id.description: Pass this to [Get Endpoint Event](/api-reference/webhooks/get-webhook-endpoint-event) for the full payload and attempt history, or to the resend endpoint to try delivery again.

event_type.description: What happened, in `resource.action` form, for example `customer.created` or `payout.paid`. Branch on this before reading the payload.

entity_id.description: The identifier of the resource the event is about, so you can correlate the event with your own records without opening the payload. It is `null` when the event carries no identifiable resource.

attempts.description: How many times we have tried to deliver this event to this endpoint, including the original send and every retry.

success.description: How many of those attempts your endpoint answered with a 2xx. Anything above zero means you have received this event at least once and should have handled it idempotently.

failed.description: How many of those attempts were rejected or never connected. A non-zero value with `success` at zero means this event has not reached you yet.

last_attempt_status.description: How the most recent attempt ended. `pending`: queued and not yet sent. `succeeded`: your endpoint answered with a 2xx. `failed`: your endpoint answered with a non-2xx or could not be reached. It is `null` when no attempt has been recorded yet.

last_attempt_http_status.description: The HTTP status code your endpoint returned on the most recent attempt. It is `null` when the connection never completed, for example on a DNS failure or a timeout, which is what distinguishes a transport failure from a rejection.

last_attempt_at.description: When the most recent attempt was made, as an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC. It is `null` when no attempt has been recorded yet.

last_attempt_error.description: Why the most recent attempt failed, as a short diagnostic string you can act on, for example a timeout or a TLS failure. It is `null` when the attempt succeeded.

WebhookEndpointEventsListResponse.description: A paginated list of events delivered to an endpoint.

items.description: The events this endpoint has been sent, newest attempt first. Each entry summarises delivery to this one endpoint; fetch the full payload and every attempt with [Get Endpoint Event](/api-reference/webhooks/get-webhook-endpoint-event).

total.description: How many distinct events this endpoint has delivery attempts for, ignoring `limit` and `offset`. Use it to decide whether another page is worth requesting.

limit.description: The page size actually applied, which is clamped to between 1 and 100 whatever you request.

offset.description: How many events were skipped before this page. Add `limit` to it to request the next page.

WebhookEventAttempt.description: A single delivery attempt for an event.

attempt_id.description: Identifies this single delivery attempt. Quote it when you contact support about a delivery you cannot account for.

attempt_no.description: Where this attempt sits in the retry sequence for the event, starting at `1` for the original send. A high number means the event has been retried repeatedly and your endpoint has been rejecting it.

status.description: How this attempt ended. `pending`: queued and not yet sent. `succeeded`: your endpoint answered with a 2xx. `failed`: your endpoint answered with a non-2xx or could not be reached, and the event is retried on a backoff.

callback_url.description: The URL this attempt was sent to, captured at send time, so an attempt made before you changed the endpoint's `url` still shows where it actually went. It is `null` on attempts recorded without a resolved destination.

http_status.description: The HTTP status code your endpoint returned. It is `null` when the request never completed, for example on a DNS failure or a timeout, which is how you tell a transport failure from a rejection.

response_snippet.description: The first part of your endpoint's response body, kept so you can see what your own handler replied without adding logging on your side. It is `null` when no response body was received.

last_error.description: Why this attempt failed, as a short diagnostic string you can act on, for example a timeout, a TLS failure, or the rejecting status code. It is `null` when the attempt succeeded.

created_at.description: When the attempt was queued, as an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC.

updated_at.description: When the attempt reached its final status, as an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC. Subtract `created_at` from it to see how long your endpoint took to answer.

WebhookEventDetail.description: A webhook event with its full payload and delivery attempts.

event_id.description: Identifies this event everywhere it appears, including as `id` inside the delivered payload, so you can use it as your deduplication key when you process a redelivery.

event_type.description: What happened, in `resource.action` form, for example `customer.created` or `payout.paid`. Branch on this before reading `payload`.

entity_type.description: The kind of resource the event is about, for example `customer`, `charge`, `payout`, `refund`, or `checkout`. It is `null` when the event carries no identifiable resource.

entity_id.description: The identifier of the resource named by `entity_type`, matching the id you would use to fetch that resource from its own endpoint. It is `null` when the event carries no identifiable resource.

created_at.description: When the event was recorded, as an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC. This is the moment the change happened, not the moment it was delivered.

payload.description: The exact JSON body sent to your endpoint, byte for byte. It wraps the resource in an envelope of `id`, `type`, `created_at`, `organization_id`, and `data`, and adds `account` when the event came from an account you own. Replay this against your handler to reproduce a delivery.

attempts.description: Every delivery attempt made for this event, newest attempt number first. Read the first entry to see the current state and the rest to see what your endpoint returned on earlier tries.

ResendWebhookEventResponse.description: The result of re-delivering an event.

status.description: Always `queued` on success. The redelivery is asynchronous, so a `queued` response means the attempt was accepted, not that your endpoint has received it; poll the event's `attempts` to see the outcome.

attempt_id.description: The new delivery attempt created by this call. Match it against the `attempts` array on [Get Event](/api-reference/webhooks/get-webhook-event) to see whether the redelivery succeeded.

DeleteWebhookEndpointResponse.description: Confirmation that an endpoint was deleted.

status.description: Always `deleted` on success. The endpoint stops receiving events immediately and its signing secret can no longer be read.

endpoint_id.description: Echoes the endpoint you deleted so you can reconcile the call against your own records.

TrialPeriod.description: The length of the free trial before the first charge, expressed as a count of time units. For example, `{ "interval": "day", "frequency": 14 }` is a 14-day trial.

interval.description: The unit of time the trial is measured in: `day`, `week`, `month`, or `year`.

frequency.description: How many `interval` units the trial lasts. For example, `interval` `day` with `frequency` `14` is a 14-day trial.

destination.description: The account to credit, or `self` to send funds back to your platform when acting as an account you own with `X-Account-Id`. The debited side is always whoever is authenticated, so there is no source field.

amount.description: Amount to move as a decimal string in `currency`, e.g. "7000.00". Always two decimal places. Must be greater than zero.

currency.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the transfer, e.g. `NGN`. Both balances must already hold this currency; a transfer never converts.

description.description: An arbitrary string attached to the transfer and returned unchanged. Useful for naming the order or invoice the share belongs to.

metadata.description: Your own key-value data, returned unchanged on the transfer. Not used by Bachs for processing.

transfer_group.description: Tags this transfer as part of a group, so several shares funded by the same charge can be reconciled together. Reuse the same value across every transfer for one charge, including a later recovery.

source.description: Whoever was debited. Your platform when sending a share to an account you own, the account when recovering one.

amount.description: The amount moved, as a decimal string in `currency`.

currency.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code the transfer moved.

status.description: Whether the funds have moved. `paid`: the balances have been updated. `pending`: the transfer exists but its movement has not been recorded yet. Derived from the underlying movement, so it never disagrees with the balances.

description.description: The description you supplied on creation.

metadata.description: The metadata you supplied on creation, returned unchanged.

transfer_group.description: The group you supplied on creation, or `null` when the transfer was not tagged.

kind.description: What this movement is. `payout` is a seller's share of a sale you made, and `manual` is a transfer you created yourself. The platform's own cut of a sale is never a transfer; read it at [Platform fees](/connect/platform-fees).

source_charge_id.description: The charge that funded this movement, when one did. Null on a transfer you created yourself, which is tied to nothing.

created_at.description: When the transfer was created, ISO 8601 in UTC.

items.description: The transfers on this page, newest first.

id.description: The platform fee's unique identifier, prefixed `pf_`.

charge.description: The charge that this fee was struck against, prefixed `ch_`.

collected_from.description: The account the fee was collected from: the seller on a destination charge, or the merchant itself on a direct charge.

earned_by.description: The platform that earned the fee.

amount.description: The fee amount, as a decimal string in `currency`.

currency.description: The currency the sale was struck in, before any conversion, as an ISO 4217 code.

amount_refunded.description: How much of this fee has been reversed. Currently always `"0.00"`: a platform fee is not reversed when its charge is refunded.

refunded.description: Whether the fee has been fully reversed. Derived from `amount_refunded` against `amount`, so it cannot disagree with them.

created_at.description: When the fee was recorded, ISO 8601 in UTC.

items.description: The platform fees on this page, newest first.

pagination.description: Pagination cursors and counts. See the Pagination guide.

code.description: Machine-readable reason the capability is not active. Branch on this rather than on `message`.

resolution.description: What has to happen for the capability to become active.
resolution.example: Contact support to re-enable this capability.

message.description: Human-readable explanation, safe to show the account holder.
message.example: This capability was disabled by the platform.

status.description: Whether the account may perform this action. `active`: enabled, and the only value that authorizes anything. `pending`: requested or submitted, awaiting review. `restricted`: not enabled, and the default. `unrequested`: the account has no record for this capability, which differs from `restricted` in that it was never asked for. `unsupported`: the account is not eligible for this capability.

requested.description: Whether the account ever requested this capability. A `restricted` capability that was requested is in progress; one that was never requested is outside the account's setup.

status_details.description: Why the capability is not active. `null` when the capability is `active`, meaning there is nothing to explain.

field.description: The field key that was rejected.

reason.description: Human-readable rejection reason, safe to show the account holder.
reason.example: The document image was too blurry to read.

AccountRequirements.description: The account-wide roll-up of outstanding requirements. Populated on single-account reads only.

eventually_due.description: Field keys required later, once a threshold or stage is reached.

past_due.description: Field keys that were required by a date now passed.

pending_verification.description: Field keys provided and being checked.

errors.description: Fields that were provided and then rejected, as distinct from fields that are missing.

entries.description: Per-field view of the same requirements, each carrying the capabilities it blocks.

values.description: Only present with `include=requirements.values`. Account-level fields and their current values, for reading back what was submitted and prefilling an edit. Sensitive fields are listed as provided and never echoed. People are returned separately under `persons`.

persons.description: One entry per person on the account, rolled up rather than split into fields. Each entry carries `id`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `dob`, `address`, `address_reference_data`, `relationship`, `id_document_provided`, and `verification_status`. Identity documents are summarised by the `id_document_provided` flag and never returned. Only present with `include=requirements.values`.

current_deadline.description: The soonest deadline across everything outstanding, for a single banner. Null when no outstanding field carries one.

fees.description: Who collects the Bachs processing fee on this account's charges.

collector.description: `bachs`: the fee comes out of the charge and the account settles net. `platform`: the platform absorbs the fee and the account settles gross. Set when the account is created and immutable afterwards.

items.description: The accounts on this page. Items never carry `capabilities` or `requirements`; read a single account for those.

limit.description: The page size used for this response.

offset.description: The offset used for this response.

requested.description: Set to `true` to request this capability for the account, which applies the configuration the capability belongs to and surfaces the requirements it needs. Requesting authorizes nothing on its own. `false` is rejected with `400 capability_unrequest_unsupported`, because there is no path to withdraw a capability once it has been requested.

AccountConfigurationOptions.description: A named persona, and the capabilities requested under it. `capabilities` omitted requests every capability that persona allows on create (never on update); `{}` requests none.

capabilities.description: Capabilities requested under this persona, keyed by name. Omitting this on create requests every capability the persona allows; omitting it on update just applies the persona and requests nothing. Send `{}` to apply the persona and request nothing, on either endpoint. An unrecognised or inactive capability name is rejected with `400 unknown_capability`.

ResponsibilitiesRequest.description: Fee arrangement for the account. Set once at creation and immutable afterwards.

fees.description: Who collects the Bachs processing fee on this account's charges. Defaults to `bachs`.

collector.description: `bachs`: the fee comes out of the charge and the account settles net. `platform`: the platform absorbs the fee on this account's charges and the account settles gross.

contact_email.description: Email address of the person or business behind the account. Trimmed and lowercased before it is stored.

display_name.description: Name you want the account listed under. Becomes the account's `name`, and is `null` until the account holder sets one during onboarding if you omit it.

first_name.description: Given name of the person you are onboarding, used to label the account before verification collects a legal name. Whitespace-only values are stored as `null`.

last_name.description: Family name of the person you are onboarding. Whitespace-only values are stored as `null`.

country.description: Two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code for the account. Decides which requirements the account is given, so set it when you already know it. Falls back to your own platform's country.

entity_type.description: What kind of legal person the account is, which together with `country` decides the requirements it is given. `company`: a registered entity, asked for registration and ownership details. `individual`: a natural person, asked only for their own identity.

configuration.description: Personas the account is being created for, keyed by name (`merchant`, `recipient`). No persona is ever applied automatically, `recipient` included. An account created with no `configuration` holds neither and cannot hold any capability. Sending an empty object is rejected with `422 VALIDATION_ERROR`; omit the field entirely for a persona-less account instead. A capability is only ever named inside the persona object it belongs to, in its `capabilities`, so naming one always names its persona in the same request; there is no way to name a capability without also naming a persona, and no way to infer one from a bare capability name. A capability nested under the wrong persona for it is rejected with `400 capability_configuration_mismatch`. There is no field to apply a configuration after creation other than naming it again on update, so decide every persona the account will ever need up front, or add one later on `POST /v1/accounts/{account_id}`. An unrecognised key is rejected with `400 invalid_configuration`.

responsibilities.description: Fee arrangement for the account. Defaults to Bachs collecting its fee out of the charge.

name.description: The action this entry governs. `payouts`: withdraw from the account's balance to a bank or wallet. `transfers`: move funds between your balance and the account's. `conversions`: convert between currencies the account holds. `connect`: create and onboard accounts of its own.

status.description: Whether the account may perform this action. `active`: enabled, and the only value that authorizes anything. `pending`: requested or submitted, awaiting review. `restricted`: not enabled, and the default. `unrequested`: no record exists for this capability, which differs from `restricted` in that it was never asked for. `unsupported`: the account is not eligible for this capability at all.

requested.description: Whether the account ever requested this capability. A `restricted` capability that was requested is in progress; one that was never requested is outside the account's setup.

status_details.description: Why the capability is not active. `null` when the capability is `active`, meaning there is nothing to explain.

items.description: Every capability applicable to the account, including ones it has never requested. Capabilities the account is not eligible to hold at all are omitted rather than returned as `unsupported`.

type.description: What the account holder is being sent to do. `onboarding`: collect everything the account still owes for the first time. `update`: revisit information already collected, which requires the account to have requirements already and otherwise fails with `400 CONNECTED_ACCOUNT_REQUIREMENTS_NOT_FOUND`.

refresh_url.description: Where the account holder is sent when the link is no longer usable, for example after it expired. Issue a fresh link from the page you point at, because the original URL cannot be revived.

return_url.description: Where the account holder is sent when they finish or abandon the flow. Arriving here is not proof that onboarding completed, so confirm from the `account.updated` event rather than from the redirect.

collection_options.description: Options carried through to the hosted flow and handed back unchanged when the link is opened. Omit it unless you were given specific keys to send.

id.description: Unique identifier for the account link.

object.description: Always `connected_account_link`, so a mixed webhook or log stream can be routed on type.

type.description: What the link was issued for, echoing the `type` you sent. `onboarding`: the account holder is walked through everything the account still owes, for the first time. `update`: the account holder revisits information already collected, which only works once the account has requirements and otherwise fails with `400 CONNECTED_ACCOUNT_REQUIREMENTS_NOT_FOUND`.

created.description: When the link was issued, ISO 8601 in UTC.

expires_at.description: When the link stops working, ISO 8601 in UTC. After this the account holder lands on your `refresh_url` instead. Read this value rather than assuming a fixed lifetime.

url.description: Send the account holder here. The URL carries a single-use credential, so deliver it over a channel you trust and keep it out of logs and analytics. It is returned only on this response and cannot be read back.

previous_link_superseded.description: `true` when issuing this link invalidated an outstanding active link of the same `type` for the account. Generating a link on every page render keeps invalidating the one you already sent, so create a link when you are about to redirect and not before.

TaskValueItem.description: One field's current value, for reading back what the account already provided and prefilling an edit form.

field.description: Canonical key for the field, the same key you submit it under.

label.description: Human-readable name for the field, safe to show the account holder verbatim.

group.description: Which onboarding section the field is shown in: `identity_verification`, `business_ownership`, `product_information`, or `bank_verification`. Note this is a coarser grouping than the `group` on a checklist field. `null` when the field maps to no section.

provided.description: Whether the account has a value for this field. A sensitive field reports `provided: true` with no `value`.

sensitive.description: When `true`, the value is never echoed back: `value` stays `null` and `display` reads `Provided`. Identity documents and bank account numbers are sensitive, so an edit form has to collect them again rather than prefill them.

value.description: The raw value, suitable for prefilling an edit form. Always `null` when `sensitive` is `true`.

display.description: One-line summary of the value for a review card. `Provided` for a sensitive field, and `null` when nothing has been provided.

reference_data.description: Resolved labels for a value that is stored as a code, such as the name behind a bank code, so a review card does not have to look them up. `null` when the field has nothing to resolve.

country.description: Two-letter ISO 3166-1 country the list was resolved for, uppercased.

banks.description: Banks you can submit as a payout destination for this country.

name.description: Bank name to show the account holder.

code.description: Code to send as `bank_code` when resolving an account or submitting a payout destination.

country.description: Two-letter ISO 3166-1 country the list was resolved for, uppercased.

providers.description: Mobile money provider names available in this country, deduplicated and in display order. Empty when the country has none.

account_number.description: The account number to look up, digits only and exactly as the account holder typed it.

bank_code.description: Code of the bank holding the account, taken from `code` on the bank list.

country.description: Two-letter ISO 3166-1 country to resolve in. Falls back to the account's country, and a country outside `NG` and `GH` comes back as `resolved: false` rather than an error.

resolved.description: Whether the account number was matched. `false` covers a wrong number, an unsupported country, and a lookup that could not be completed, so read `message` to tell them apart. A `false` here is not an HTTP error.

account_name.description: Name registered on the account. Show it back for confirmation before you submit the payout destination. `null` when `resolved` is `false`.

account_number.description: The account number as it is held on record, which can be normalised from what you sent. `null` when `resolved` is `false`.

message.description: Why the lookup did not resolve, safe to show the account holder. `null` on a successful match.

CreatePayoutRequest.description: Send money to a registered destination. Exactly one of `amount` or `quote_id` is required, never both and never neither. `amount` funds a same-currency payout; `quote_id` funds a cross-currency payout, since the quote already fixes both sides.

destination.description: The ID of a payout destination belonging to your account. The destination must be usable (`is_usable: true`).

amount.description: The amount the destination should receive, as a decimal string (e.g. "5000.00"), in the destination's currency. The fee is charged on top of this amount, not deducted from it. Omit when supplying `quote_id`.

quote_id.description: A quote ID from Create Payout Quote. Required for cross-currency payouts, where the source currency differs from the destination's currency. Omit `amount` when supplying this field.

reference.description: Your own reference for this payout, up to 128 characters. Omit it and the payout has none; use the payout's `id` to track it.

metadata.description: Arbitrary key-value data to attach to the payout.

CreatePayoutDestinationRequest.description: Register where money should land. Accepts both the field names this surface has always used and newer aliases, so a caller never has to know which generation of the API it is talking to. Where a legacy name and its alias overlap, the newer name wins.

name.description: User-friendly name for this destination.

label.description: Alias for `name`. `name` wins if both are sent.

currency.description: Currency code this destination accepts (e.g., 'NGN', 'USD', 'USDT_TRC20').

type.description: Type of payout destination: `bank_account`, `mobile_money`, or `crypto_wallet`. Inferred from `currency` when omitted.

destination_type.description: Alias for `type`. `type` wins if both are sent.

account_number.description: Bank account number. Required for bank_account destinations.

bank_code.description: Bank code or routing number. Required for bank_account destinations.

account_name.description: Accepted for compatibility and ignored, because the account holder name is always resolved from the bank.

bank_name.description: Accepted for compatibility and ignored, because the bank name is always resolved from the bank.

phone_number.description: Phone number for the mobile money account. Required for mobile_money destinations.

mobile_provider.description: Mobile money provider (e.g., 'MTN', 'Vodafone'). Required for mobile_money destinations.

wallet_address.description: Cryptocurrency wallet address. Required for crypto_wallet destinations.

network.description: Blockchain network. Optional when the currency already names its network (e.g. USDT_TRC20).

metadata.description: Additional custom metadata to associate with this destination.

UpdatePayoutDestinationRequest.description: The one update a destination allows. `name` and `is_default` alone are safe: a rename touches no routing column, and the default can only ever be one of your own approved destinations. Sending any field below restates the destination in full, the same shape as `POST`; omitted routing fields fall back to what is already stored. Changing an account number, bank code, wallet, network or phone number this way sends the destination back for review, because the approval it holds was granted for the details it is being asked to leave behind.

name.description: The new name for this destination.

is_default.description: Make this the destination a payout schedule pays out to for its currency. Setting it demotes the previous default; false clears it. Ignored if this request also changes where money lands and that change sends the destination back for review.

currency.description: Currency code this destination accepts (e.g., 'NGN', 'USD', 'USDT_TRC20').

destination_type.description: Alias for `type`. `type` wins if both are sent.

account_name.description: Account holder name. Unlike registration, an update trusts the name it is given.

phone_number.description: Phone number for the mobile money account.

network.description: Blockchain network. Optional when the currency already names its network (e.g. USDT_TRC20).

metadata.description: Additional custom metadata to associate with this destination.

PayoutDestinationResponse.description: Response containing payout destination details (bank account, mobile money, or crypto wallet).

id.description: Unique identifier for this payout destination. Use this ID when creating payouts.

name.description: User-friendly name for this destination. Helps you identify destinations in your system.

type.description: Type of payout destination: `bank_account`, `mobile_money`, or `crypto_wallet`. Determines which fields are populated.

currency.description: Currency code this destination accepts (e.g., 'NGN', 'USD', 'USDT_TRC20'). Payouts to this destination must use this currency.

status.description: Review status. `pending_review`: awaiting review, not usable yet. `approved`: cleared for payouts. `rejected`: permanently unusable, register a new destination instead.

status_reason.description: Free-text reason set by review, populated when the destination is rejected. Null while pending or approved.

is_usable.description: Whether this destination can be used for a payout right now. True only when `status` is `approved` and the destination has not been deactivated.

is_default.description: Whether a payout schedule pays out to this destination for its currency. Set it with `PATCH /v1/payouts/destinations/{destination_id}`.

account_number.description: Bank account number. Only populated for bank_account destinations.

account_name.description: Account holder name as resolved from the bank. Only populated for bank_account destinations.

bank_code.description: Bank code or routing number. Only populated for bank_account destinations.

bank_name.description: Full name of the bank. Only populated for bank_account destinations.

phone_number.description: Phone number associated with the mobile money account. Only populated for mobile_money destinations.

mobile_provider.description: Mobile money provider (e.g., 'MTN', 'Vodafone'). Only populated for mobile_money destinations.

wallet_address.description: Cryptocurrency wallet address. Only populated for crypto_wallet destinations.

network.description: Blockchain network (e.g., 'TRC20', 'ERC20'). Only populated for crypto_wallet destinations. May be included in currency code (e.g., 'USDT_TRC20').

reviewed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when this destination was last reviewed by an admin. Null until reviewed.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when this destination was created.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when this destination was last updated.

PayoutDestinationListResponse.description: Paginated list of configured payout destinations. `total` counts every matching destination, not just the ones on this page.

total.description: Total number of destinations matching the query, across all pages.

limit.description: The `limit` used for this page of results.

offset.description: The `offset` used for this page of results.

DeletePayoutDestinationResponse.description: Confirmation that a destination was deactivated.

id.description: The ID of the destination that was deactivated.

deleted.description: Always true. Payouts already sent against this destination are unaffected.

RequirementEntry.description: One outstanding requirement and what it holds up. The buckets say what is missing; this says what breaks while it is. Prefer this over the buckets when an account holds more than one capability.

status.description: The bucket this entry is in.

restricts_capabilities.description: Capabilities this field blocks. Empty when no capability the account holds requires it.

errors.description: Verification or rejection errors for this field.

resolution.description: Who can act on this field. `api`: yours to supply, through the account update or the persons subresource. `review`: already provided and sitting with us, so re-sending it achieves nothing. Treat an unrecognized value as not yours to resolve.

deadline.description: When this field must be resolved by, if a deadline was set.

PersonRelationship.description: Role flags. One person is commonly several of these at once, which is why they are flags on one person rather than separate collections.

representative.description: The person who controls the account and acts for it.

owner.description: A beneficial owner at or above the ownership threshold.

director.description: `true` when the person sits on the board of the company behind the account. It is independent of the other flags, so setting it does not clear `representative`, `owner` or `executive`.

executive.description: `true` when the person is a senior manager of the company behind the account. It is independent of the other flags, so setting it does not clear `representative`, `owner` or `director`.

title.description: The person's job title at the company behind the account, for example `Founder` or `Chief Financial Officer`, or `null` when none was given.

PersonVerification.description: What has been established about this person. How it was established is not reported.

document_provided.description: Whether an identity document is held.

failure_reason.description: Written for display to the account holder.

id.description: The person's identifier, prefixed `per_`. Requirement keys are anchored to it, so `persons.per_3a91c0d7.id_document` names exactly who owes a document.

first_name.description: The person's given name as recorded, or `null` when it has not been supplied yet. It is the name their identity document is checked against.

last_name.description: The person's family name as recorded, or `null` when it has not been supplied yet. It is checked against the identity document alongside `first_name`.

address.description: The person's residential address, carrying the `line1`, `city`, `state`, `postal_code` and `country` keys that were written, or `null` when no address has been supplied. It is stored whole, so a later write replaces it rather than merging into it.

phone.description: The contact number recorded for this person, returned exactly as it was sent, or `null` when none has been supplied.

email.description: The email address recorded for this person, or `null` when none has been supplied. It belongs to the person, not to the account, so it differs from the account's `contact_email`.

id_number_provided.description: `true` when a government ID number is held for this person, `false` when none has been supplied. The number itself is write-only and never returned, so this flag is how you tell whether you still need to collect one.

created_at.description: When the person was added to the account, ISO 8601 in UTC.

updated_at.description: When the person record last changed, ISO 8601 in UTC. A verification outcome we record moves it as well as your own writes, so do not read it as the time of your last edit.

items.description: The account's persons for this page, oldest first, each carrying the same shape as [reading one person](/connect/accounts#persons). The order is stable, so paging with `offset` neither repeats nor skips anyone.

total.description: How many persons the account has in total, not how many came back on this page. Compare it against `offset` plus the length of `items` to know whether another page is waiting.

limit.description: How many persons a page returns at most, echoing the `limit` you sent. It defaults to 50 and is capped at 100; anything outside 1 to 100 is rejected with `422`.

offset.description: How many persons were skipped before this page, echoing the `offset` you sent. Add `limit` to it to ask for the next page, and stop once it reaches `total`.

PersonWriteRequest.description: On edit, omitted keys are left alone and an explicit `null` clears the field. Naming one relationship flag leaves the others as they were.

first_name.description: The person's given name as it appears on their government ID, since a mismatch against the document is the most common reason identity verification is rejected. On an update, omitting this key leaves the stored value alone and sending it as `null` clears it.

last_name.description: The person's family name as it appears on their government ID, checked against the document alongside `first_name`. On an update, omitting this key leaves the stored value alone and sending it as `null` clears it.

address.description: The person's residential address, as an object with `line1`, `city`, `state` and `country` (two-letter ISO 3166-1), plus an optional `postal_code`. It is written whole rather than merged, so send every key you want kept; on an update, omitting this key leaves the stored address alone and sending it as `null` clears it.

phone.description: A contact number for this person, kept with their identity record and passed on when their identity is checked, 32 characters or fewer. On an update, omitting this key leaves the stored value alone and sending it as `null` clears it.

email.description: This person's own email address, separate from the account's `contact_email`, and used for correspondence about their verification rather than the account's. It must be a valid address or the request fails with `422`; on an update, omitting this key leaves the stored value alone and sending it as `null` clears it.

id_number.description: The person's government ID number. It is write-only: it is never echoed back, and the response reports `id_number_provided` instead. On an update, omitting this key leaves the stored number alone and sending it as `null` clears it.

configuration.description: Personas to apply, and capabilities to request under them, the same nested shape as creation. Naming a persona here, with or without a capability nested under its `capabilities, is what applies it if the account does not already have it: an account can start recipient-only and be given `merchant` later this way. Unlike creation, an omitted `capabilities` here never blanket-requests; it only applies the persona. A capability nested under the wrong persona for it is rejected with `400 capability_configuration_mismatch`. Only names set to `true` are acted on; any name set to `false` fails the whole request with `400 capability_unrequest_unsupported`. Capabilities the account already holds are unaffected, and an omitted map changes nothing.

display_name.description: The account's public name. Omit to leave it unchanged.

contact_email.description: Where onboarding correspondence for the account is sent. Omit to leave it unchanged.

fields.description: Requirement values, keyed by the field keys the account's requirements name: `persons`, `company.*`, `business_profile.*`, `payout_destination`, `tos_acceptance.*`. Omit to change nothing.

balance_currencies.description: Which currencies the account holds, keyed by currency code. Holding a currency decides what the account settles in; a one-time checkout can be priced in any supported currency regardless. A recurring checkout is the exception and must be priced in a held currency, so set this before the account sells subscriptions in its own market. A new account holds only USD. Send `true` to add a currency and `false` to remove one. Omitthe field and nothing changes. USD is always held and cannot be removed. A currency Bachs cannot settle in is rejected with `400`.

UpdateAccountRequest.description: The one account write. Set contact details, request capabilities and satisfy requirement fields in a single call. Anything you leave out is unchanged.

PayoutScheduleRequest.description: Set when a currency pays out. Replaces the currency's schedule rather than patching it: a field you omit is cleared, not kept.

interval.description:
How often this currency pays out.

- `manual`: nothing is paid out automatically. The balance stays put until you call Create Payout.
- `instant`: about a minute after funds settle, so several times on a busy day and not at all on a quiet one. Collections settling close together are paid out together, in one payout carrying one fee.
- `daily`: once a day, at `anchor_hour_utc`.
- `weekly`: once a week, on `weekly_anchor`, at `anchor_hour_utc`.
- `monthly`: once a month, on `monthly_anchor`, at `anchor_hour_utc`.

weekly_payout_days.description: Weekdays a weekly payout lands on. Listing more than one means more than one payout a week: `["monday", "thursday"]` pays twice. Defaults to `["monday"]`. Sending it on any other interval is rejected rather than ignored, so a schedule never quietly loses the days you asked for.

monthly_payout_days.description: Days of the month a monthly payout lands on, each `1` to `31`. Listing more than one means more than one payout a month. 29, 30 and 31 land on the last day of a shorter month, so `[31]` pays on the 31st of January and the 28th of February. Defaults to `[1]`. Sending it on any other interval is rejected.

anchor_hour_utc.description: The UTC hour to run at, `0` to `23`. Defaults to `10`. Ignored by `manual` and `instant`.

payout_currency.description: The currency to deliver the money in, in ISO 4217 format. Defaults to the balance currency. Setting it to something else converts each run at the rate of the day it runs, and is available out of USD and stablecoin balances only. Converting out of a local settlement currency is rejected here rather than at run time.

minimum_amount.description: A floor for a run, as a decimal string (e.g. "5000.00") in the balance currency. A run whose eligible total is below it pays nothing and the money rolls into the next run. Omit for no floor.

PayoutScheduleResponse.description: The payout schedule for one currency of one account.

currency.description: The balance currency this schedule governs, in ISO 4217 format. Each currency is scheduled independently.

payout_currency.description: The currency the money is delivered in. Equal to `currency` unless the schedule converts, in which case each run is quoted at the rate of the day it runs.

How often this currency pays out.

- `manual`: nothing is paid out automatically. The balance stays put until you call Create Payout.
- `instant`: about a minute after funds settle, so several times on a busy day and not at all on a quiet one. Collections settling close together are paid out together, in one payout carrying one fee.
- `daily`: once a day, at `anchor_hour_utc`.
- `weekly`: once a week, on `weekly_anchor`, at `anchor_hour_utc`.
- `monthly`: once a month, on `monthly_anchor`, at `anchor_hour_utc`.

monthly_payout_days.description: Days of the month a monthly payout lands on, each `1` to `31`. Listing more than one means more than one payout a month. 29, 30 and 31 land on the last day of a shorter month, so `[31]` pays on the 31st of January and the 28th of February. Null on every other interval.

anchor_hour_utc.description: The UTC hour a scheduled run happens, `0` to `23`. Defaults to `10`. Null on `manual` and `instant`, which have no schedule.

minimum_amount.description: The floor a run has to reach before it pays anything, as a decimal string in `currency`. A run below it pays nothing and the money rolls into the next run. Null means no floor.

next_run_at.description: When the next scheduled run is due, in ISO 8601. Always null on `manual` and `instant`: one pays out nothing and the other reacts to funds settling rather than to a clock, so neither has a next run to show.

last_run_at.description: When a run last happened, in ISO 8601, whether or not it moved money. Null until the first run.

last_withdrawal_id.description: The payout created by the last run that moved money. Read it with Get Payout. Null until a run has paid out.

disabled_reason.description: Why the currency was set back to `manual` by itself, including the error from the run that tripped it. Null when that never happened.
disabled_reason.example: Auto-payout paused after 3 consecutive failures. Last error: destination rejected in review
